column3: “The earth” identifies the otherwise unstated object.
“Palaces” specifies houses; “for defense” supplies the purpose of demolition.
The Chaldeans are made the subject of coming to fight; the Hebrew describes people coming to fight with the Chaldeans.
“Restore ... from captivity” renders turning back captivity.
Sin and rebellion are combined in the second forgiveness clause.
“This city” identifies the subject; “for it” in the first good-deeds clause replaces “to them.”
The separate mention of an inhabitant is not explicit.
Bride and bridegroom are reversed; restoring the land from captivity renders turning back its captivity.
The closing “all the days” is not explicit.
The clause about having no son is moved after the mention of Levites.
“Restore them from captivity” renders turning back captivity.
